title: Baba Ganoush
subtitle: Smoky charred aubergine dip with tahini and lemon
excerpt: Baba ganoush is a Middle Eastern dip made from aubergines charred directly over a flame or under a grill until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses into something smoky and silky. Mixed with tahini and lemon, it is one of the best things you can do with an aubergine.
sourceNotes: Baba ganoush is found across the Levant and is particularly associated with Lebanese and Syrian cuisine. The name is thought to translate roughly as 'pampered daddy', a reference to the care taken in its preparation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a few hours ahead to let the flavours settle. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: The smokiness comes from charring the aubergine skin until it is completely black. On a gas hob, hold the aubergine directly over the flame and turn it regularly with tongs. Under a grill, get it as close to the element as possible and turn every 10 minutes. The inside must be completely soft and collapsed.

Prick the aubergines all over with a fork. Char them directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill for 30 to 40 minutes, turning regularly, until the skin is completely black and the flesh is completely soft.
Transfer to a colander and leave for 10 minutes until cool enough to handle. Peel off and discard all the charred skin.
Put the flesh into a blender or food processor with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and olive oil. Blend until smooth. Alternatively, chop and mash roughly by hand for a more textured result.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt. Spoon into a wide bowl, drizzle with olive oil and scatter with smoked paprika and parsley.

items.cause: Charred skin got mixed in with the flesh.
items.fix: Remove every piece of black skin before blending.

items.cause: Aubergine not charred enough on the outside.
items.fix: Go further. The skin should be completely black.
